svg.text: A floor, a wall and a ceiling make half a corridor. Mirror them for the other half. A rib drops in every 4 m without changing any of the three.
Nine facets per half instead of twenty-two. Chamfers, not steps. Every vertex is a multiple of 0.125 m (4 map units at 32 u/m).
Both halves plus a rib at a station.
Four 1 m texture repeats per bay.
The rib runs floor to ceiling on a battered base.
it rises outward and the player could
The rib runs floor to ceiling. Its
toe is vertical to knee height, so
the capsule never meets a slope low.
to buy the rib base a 0.50 m flare,
with the toes still 4.00 m apart.
HALF A CORRIDOR — THE THREE PIECES
Each is a separate reusable brush. They mate at the two ringed points, so any one can be swapped for a special without touching the others.
top face is the walking surface at Y = 0
swap for grating, a hatch or a ramp
swap for a service run, light or hatch
The two pieces above are plain slabs. All the shape is in the wall,
which is why it is the only one of the three worth drawing large.
Mating points: floor meets wall at (2.5, 0); wall meets ceiling
at (2.25, 3.75). Both are ringed on the assembled section above.
Panel zone 1.25 – 2.50 m is the only part that swaps.
Facets 1 and 3 rise outward low enough that the capsule could try to
stand on them, so both are steeper than the 45° floor_max_angle default.
The 45° chamfers are all overhangs, which cannot be stood on at all.
Wall solids back to x = 3.50, so the piece is 0.50 – 1.25 m thick and
tiles against the next bay with no coplanar overlap.
Five facets. Drops in without altering the wall.
toe sits on the lane line — opposite toes ARE the 4.00 m clear width
wall behind (dashed) — proud at every height
toe is vertical to knee height, then batters 0.50 m back onto the shaft · 51.34°
Each replaces the 1.25 – 2.50 m panel and nothing else, so the piece still mates.
Flat panel. The default and the cheapest.
Panel set back 0.125 m behind a 45 chamfered reveal.
Recessed field with slats. Honest home for a wall hatch.
Panel becomes glazing on a chamfered reveal.
Panel zone opens full height; needs a rib either side.
Floor and ceiling swap the same way: a grating strip, a service run, a light panel, a sealed hatch.
The corridor envelope never changes, so nothing downstream has to be re-measured.
REVISION 06 / BUILT AND LIT — one 24.5 m run, 151 brushes, 1,037 validation checks pass · corners and the circuit remain open
